title: A low-rank subspace of LLM representations carries most of their brain alignment
summary: A Dartmouth preprint studied which language-model features predict human neural responses during naturalistic listening. Across three intracranial/fMRI datasets and six model conditions, reduced-rank regression recovered full linear encoding performance with about 1–3% of embedding dimensions. These directions differed from the embeddings’ principal variance axes and transferred across held-out participants, less strongly across datasets. This summary is limited to the abstract and affiliation/date metadata of the October 29, 2026 preprint. It concerns measured brain–model alignment, not proof that brains use the same representations.
ai_technology: Autoregressive and masked language models with ridge reduced-rank regression

evidence.tested: Linear encoding of observed intracranial/fMRI responses, reduced-rank analysis and transfer across held-out participants.
evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
evidence.ai_role: LLM representations are the predictors of neural activity; reduced-rank regression identifies the brain-predictive subspace.
